findings.text: the section says "The local lane was excluded twice for one cause. Its reasons were `context-fit: …` and `competence: context-window-exceeded`", but every one of the four cited pick-timing records for `an-admission-pass-reads-each-project-once` carries an `exclusions` list holding only three `codex` rows with `reason_code: "reserved-lane"` (`gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol`) and no local-lane row at all, and the record's exclusions are built from every candidate carrying any reason (`reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:446`, written out at `:135–145` with the reason code taken as the text before the colon), so the instrument the section cites would have recorded `context-fit` and `competence` rows had they existed — `offered` was empty and `fallback_reason` names `default-backend-ineligible`, i.e. the refusal came from no default-backend candidate being in the scan

findings.reason: the mechanism as written cannot produce its own case 2, so a node implementing it as described would find the move unreachable and either report a blocker or widen the change beyond the section's stated scope.
findings.text: the third deliverable says a `refuse` with every candidate removed on context alone "is treated like a fallback for `_reroute_oversized_request`. It moves the request to the widest fitting permitted lane", but `widest_fitting_candidate` admits only candidates whose `reasons` list is empty (`reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:639-645`), and in the state the deliverable names every candidate carries a context reason by definition, while the reserved lane in the cited records carries `reserved-lane`; `usable` is therefore empty, `chosen is None`, and `_reroute_oversized_request` raises the oversized shortfall refusal instead of moving anything — the same wall the plan inspects on the waiver side is unremoved on the reroute side

findings.reason: a case that passes on a hand-built snapshot proves the gate opens but not that any refuse the picker actually returns can be routed, which is the claim the section exists to make.
findings.text: case 2 ("The same node, with the picker stubbed to answer `refuse`, is moved to codex by the dispatch reroute") is satisfiable only because the test hands the reroute a candidate set built by the stub; on the real path the reroute's own scan excludes every candidate carrying a reason, so the case passes on data the code under test cannot generate, and the declared control ("Restoring the fallback-only gate around the reroute fails the second") does not distinguish the real refusal state from the stubbed one

findings.reason: two of the four cases cannot distinguish a working guard from an absent one, and the `--local` arm is the one that protects a named lane from being moved, so an unfalsifiable arm leaves the section's most consequential exclusion unmeasured.
findings.text: the done-when says "shows four things" and "Two negative controls each make one case fail", leaving case 3 ("A node above every lane's window is refused with its shortfall, as now. A node whose local exclusion includes a competence reason other than context overflow is not offered codex") and case 4 ("A node dispatched with `--local` is refused as now and not moved") without a control, and case 4 asserts behaviour that is identical on the unfixed code, so no mutation can make it fail
